root_cause: Text.append_tokens appended raw token strings to self._text without passing them through strip_control_codes, unlike Text.__init__ and Text.append which sanitize. Control codes such as '\r' then stay in the plain text; wrap/divide computes line offsets from a string whose line structure no longer matches the span offsets, and Text.divide's binary search indexes past the end of line_ranges, raising IndexError when a styled token containing '\r\n' is printed at a width that forces wrapping.
best_solution: In rich/text.py::Text.append_tokens, add `content = strip_control_codes(content)` as the first statement inside the `for content, style in tokens:` loop, before append_text and before the span length is computed, so span offsets and _length match the sanitized text (strip_control_codes is already imported in text.py). Reasoning from the statement: 'exception in append_tokens' with no other detail means append_tokens violates an invariant its sibling methods keep; diff it against Text.append / Text.__init__, which both call strip_control_codes, and apply the same sanitization.

generalizable_lesson: When the statement is only a PR title plus an issue link ('Fixed exception in X') and the issue text is unavailable, do not invent an input like None. Compare X with its sibling methods that do the same job (append vs append_tokens, __init__ vs a bulk constructor) and copy any sanitization or normalization they apply but X skips. Then try realistic hostile inputs (control chars like '\r', '\t', '\x1b', empty strings, very long lines, narrow wrap widths) through the public render path until something crashes. Never delete state updates such as a length/cache assignment to make an error go away.
acceptable_alternatives: Any change that strips control codes from each token's content before it is appended and before its span end is computed works, e.g. `append_text(strip_control_codes(content))` with the span using the stripped length, or building the sanitized list up front. Stripping only the final joined plain text would desync span offsets and is not equivalent.
